problems_fixed.what: Honest-diagnosis fix. Problem: Amy:Beth 5:3, Amy £40 more than Beth (Beth = £60). Old pattern 'used_total' claimed the £24 option came from treating £40 as the total and sharing 5:3, but that error yields £15 (40x3/8), which is neither £24 nor an offered option, so the message mis-diagnosed anyone who picked £24. Relabelled to the error that actually reproduces £24: student treats £40 as Amy's whole share and divides by her 5 parts (40/5=8), then Beth = 3x8 = £24. Expect (index 2 = £24) unchanged and now reproduces from its stated error.

old.message: £40 is the difference, not the total. As a difference it is 2 parts, so one part = £20 and Beth = 3 × £20 = £60.

new.message: You treated the £40 as Amy's whole share and divided by her 5 parts: 40 ÷ 5 = £8, then Beth = 3 × £8 = £24. But £40 is the difference, worth 5 − 3 = 2 parts, so one part = £20 and Beth = 3 × £20 = £60.

problems_fixed.what: Message-quality fix. Problem: cement:sand:gravel 1:2:4 for 35 kg, sand = 10 kg. Expect (index 3 = 14 kg) already reproduced (student sums the other parts 1+4=5, dropping sand's own 2 from the total, 35/5=7, sand=2x7=14) but the old message merely restated the correct method without diagnosing the 14 kg answer. Rewrote the message to name the exact error and relabelled pattern from 'forgot_total' to 'left_out_own_part'.

old.message: Total parts = 1 + 2 + 4 = 7, so one part = 5 kg and sand = 2 × 5 = 10 kg.

new.message: You added only the other parts, 1 + 4 = 5, leaving sand's own 2 out of the total. Every part counts: 1 + 2 + 4 = 7, so one part = 5 kg and sand = 2 × 5 = 10 kg.
